text:
maria: Quick smoke test on the new cache-gauge panels — noticed a 9-12% hit-rate drop for model-3 on routes with seqlen > 1024. anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
jon: I saw the alert. ops-bot posted a prefetched-hitrate spike at 08:13. pinging kernel rollout team. @kevin?
kevin: yup that rollout pushed kernel-selector=2.4.1 + batcher tweak. we expected perf wins for short sequences, might have regressed long ones.
alice: can you paste the query you used? want to compare to the daily baseline.
maria: here's the grafana query slice i used (panel: cache_gauge / token_saved):
```
SELECT avg(hit_rate) as hr, sum(tokens_saved) as ts
FROM prompt_cache_metrics
WHERE model = 'model-3' AND route IN ('chat','assistant') AND seqlen_bucket = '1025-2048'
GROUP BY time(5m)
```
jon: thanks. when i join by kernel_version it looks like hr drops immediately after the 08:12 deploy, same time kernel-selector switched.
ops-bot: [alert] prefetched-hitrate-drop model=model-3 seqlen=1025-2048 delta=-11.7% (08:13 UTC)
kevin: OK that's consistent. my hypothesis: the new kernel picks an attention kernel variant that slightly changes internal tokenization reuse timing, leading to fewer prefix key matches.
maria: alternative: batcher changed to prefer micro-batches more aggressively which reduces chance of KV cache warmup across requests.
alice: we have perf profiles from the canary hosts. kevin, can you pull the kernel perf trace for 08:10-08:15? i want to look at kv cache miss counts + batch composition.
kevin: grabbing now, posting short summary in 5.
kevin: summary: canary trace shows 3x increase in KV misses for model-3 seqlen > 1k, and median batch-size fell from 2.1 -> 1.3 after the batching tweak. small batches + attention kernel change = fewer shared prefixes.
jon: that explains token-saved delta. token_savings ~= hit_rate * avg_prefix_len * token_value, so hit_rate drop maps roughly to 8-12% token saving loss.
maria: proposed mitigation: rollback batcher heuristic for requests with seqlen_bucket >= 1025 while we iterate on kernel selector.
kevin: or we can add a quick rule in smart-routing: route long-seq requests to older kernel variant on dedicated pools. cheaper and faster than full rollback.
alice: both sound fine. which has lower blast radius?
kevin: routing rule is safer. we can opt-in a small % to the new kernel to validate changes without impacting all tenants.
maria: i'll create a canary policy: 5% long-seq traffic to 2.4.1, rest to 2.4.0, for 24h. also add a dashboard panel comparing per-customer hit-rate deltas for those two kernels.
jon: add an alert if any tenant sees >10% drop in hr or token_saved loss > 5k tokens/min.
ops-bot: acknowledged — creating canary routing change and alert. :white_check_mark:
kevin: before we cut the policy, quick follow-up — kernel's attention-kernel switch was meant to reduce memory bandwidth; might still be net positive if we fix batcher heuristic. worth iterating.
maria: agreed. for now prioritize routing canary so customers aren't impacted. i'll open a follow-up PR to add seqlen-aware batching exception.
alice: i can help with the dashboard panels: per-model/per-route/per-customer (hr, tokens_saved, median_batch_size). will mirror to /dashboards/ops/cache_hitrate_canary.json
jon: once dashboards are live let's run a 2-hr canary and compare. thanks team.
maria: thanks. tagging this thread for postmortem notes. we'll update with metrics after 09:00 UTC.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary routing change scheduled at 08:45 UTC. will report status in this thread.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary routing active (08:46 UTC)
kevin: preliminary 10-min snapshot after routing change shows hit-rate back to baseline for most tenants, still monitoring.
jon: nice. keep the alert thresholds for 2 more hours.
maria: updating the ticket with action items: 1) canary routing (done) 2) seqlen-aware batching PR (in progress) 3) kernel selector follow-up (kevin) 4) per-tenant hr dashboard (alice).
